text: A lens computes the 2D Fourier transform of an image essentially in the time it takes light to cross a focal length (nanoseconds for a 10 cm lens), for any input image and with no programming.
explanation: True: the book states a lens performs the 2D transform in the light-transit time and for any image content without programming, versus roughly 10 microseconds for a CPU FFT of a 1000x1000 image. The parallelism and instantaneity are exactly what make the lens the original 'photonic computer.'
